I5.read: with prototypes GLM still said wide (same as I4 without prototypes). Prototypes did not flip it to unknown.

i4_i5_branch.interpretation: Adding canonical prototypes did NOT flip GLM to unknown. Per the frozen decision table this is the 'genuine contextual-classification limitation' branch -- stronger evidence than I4 alone that the I4 failure is not mere contract underspecification. GLM keys on column-spread (products across -> wide); the macro keys on month-orientation (months down -> long); neither keys on the canonical-structure match (neither prototype matches -> unknown).

summary: I5 FAILS as run: GLM said wide even with the two canonical prototypes, the same label it gave on I4 without them. The contrastive probe did not isolate a contract-underspecification fix; instead it strengthens the contextual-classification-limitation reading (n=1, with the cross-language caveat). Recorded as-is; pass criteria not relaxed. I1/I2/I3 frozen PASS and I4 FAIL unchanged; I5 graded separately (stage i5).
caveats: n=1, no seed control: a single I5 sample. Reliability unmeasured.

Cross-language: English prototypes, Finnish target. A matched-language follow-up would be cleaner; the language difference is a caveat on the inference (though GLM is multilingual and the structure is language-independent).
The I3-mechanism hypothesis (token-absence-driven) stays a hypothesis; I5 does not isolate it.
